title: text_track output
description: Contract between the text_track child subprocess (tortured-phrases screen) and the pipeline. The parent validates structurally (see agent._validate_text_track_output) and injects findings_rows only from a valid object; anything else is recorded as track_output_invalid with ZERO findings injected. Every row arrives QUARANTINED: severity is never accusatory at this boundary.

ran.description: True only when the dictionary loaded AND paper text was actually read and scanned. False on every refusal -- and the report then keeps the blanket no-tortured-phrase-screen note rather than the scope note.

refusal_subtype.description: Distinct refusal states, per the house invariant: fingerprints_missing (installation property -- the dictionary could not load) != no_text_source (directory property -- no text-bearing file at all) != text_unreadable (file property -- sources exist but none yielded text; the shape of a scanned, never-OCR'd or corrupt paper). null when ran is True.

text_source.description: Which source in paper_text's fallback chain the screen actually read -- provenance discipline; a null accompanies a refusal.

result.description: The full detect_tortured_phrases result (quarantined), for the run directory -- not for the editorial prompt, which gets only findings_rows (summary-only payload keeps paid stage-2 tokens flat).

findings_rows.description: Rows shaped for findings.schema.json findings[], one per FAMILY that fired (aggregate rows: the signal is the count of distinct fingerprints, not any single match). The parent re-checks each: technique must be tortured_phrases and severity must be indeterminate or consistent (the quarantine leaves no other legal value at this boundary).
